blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines may not achieve full electrification until 2033, five years later than the government’s target, Camarines Sur Rep. Arnie Fuentebella said Wednesday. Fuentebella said connecting remote rural areas to the electric grid could cost as much as P67 billion, with funding shortfalls potentially delaying the National Electrification Administration’s (NEA) rollout. He made the remarks on the House of Representatives floor in response to Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Elago, who asked, “When will we achieve nearly 100 percent electrification?” “We need P67 billion, and it will be done by 2033. Because of budgetary constraints… that’s why NEA […]...
